title: Flip Game II
summary: Given a string of '+' and '-', determine if the first player can ensure a win by flipping consecutive '++' to '--' until no more moves are possible.
statement: Given a string of '+' and '-', determine if the first player can ensure a win by flipping consecutive '++' to '--' until no more moves are possible.
constraints: Players alternate changing one '++' pair to '--'. Return whether the first player can force a win when the player with no move loses.
hints: A flip divides one consecutive run of plus signs into independent left and right subgames.
Assign each run length a Grundy number: the mex of left-Grundy XOR right-Grundy over every flip position.
Build grundy[length] from smaller lengths, XOR the values for every plus run separated by minus signs, and return whether the total is nonzero.
The Sprague-Grundy XOR rule combines independent impartial games and avoids enumerating exponentially many whole strings.
editorial: Each minus sign separates moves into independent plus runs. Flipping positions i,i+1 inside a run of length L leaves subruns of lengths i and L-i-2. Their game value is the XOR of previously computed Grundy numbers; the current value is the smallest nonnegative number not reachable by one move. XORing all run values determines whether the whole position is winning. The independent oracle recursively explores and memoizes every reachable short generated string.

tests.explanation: Flipping the middle pair leaves +--+, which has no reply, so the first player can force a win.
There is no legal first move, so the first player loses.
